newsitem.title: LEBANON: Beirut t-bill issue raises 465 bln pounds.
newsitem.headline: Beirut t-bill issue raises 465 bln pounds.

text.p: Lebanon's weekly treasury bill issue of May 15 raised 465 billion Lebanese pounds, according to finance ministry results issued on Monday.
The previous issue raised 411.6 billion pounds.
The issue posted a nominal surplus of subscription against maturity of 171 billion pounds. It raised the following amounts (in billion of pounds, previous week in brackets):
The central bank said only 10 percent of all competitive bids -- those made by Lebanese institutions -- were accepted up to the discount rate and yield for three-month and six-month bills.
Acceptance for competitive bids for 12-month bills was also restricted to 30 percent for the first time in six weeks, it said.

It also restricted the acceptance of non-competitive bids -- those made by private individuals and foreign investors -- for the shorter-term bills, approving 10 percent up to the discount rate and yield for both three-month and six-month bills.
All non-competitive bids for 12-month bills were accepted while all competitive and non-competitive bids for 24-month bills were accepted,the Bank said.
The Lebanese pound closed at 1,542 to the U.S. dollar on Monday from 1,543 a week earlier and 1,576.5 a year ago.
